sections.title: The spelling -lk
paragraphs: The letters -lk have two ways to sound. In most cases, you hear just one sound as in (walk) /wɔːk/. To (walk) /wɔːk/ means to move on your feet. In other words, you say both letters together. The group makes two different sounds in English.

sections.title: How to say -lk
paragraphs: To make the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft back roof of your mouth. Stop the air for a moment, then let it burst out with no voice. For the second sound, first touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth so air flows around the sides. Then lift the back of your tongue to burst out the air. Feel your throat stay quiet.

sections.title: Spelling rules for -lk
paragraphs: The letters -lk make one sound when the first letter is a silent letter, meaning you write it but do not say it. You hear this after certain vowels, as in (talk) /tɔːk/. In other words, you pronounce both consonants together. You hear this cluster at the end of words like (milk) /mɪlk/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with -lk
paragraphs: Do not pronounce the first consonant when it must stay quiet. Many learners try to say every written letter in words like (walk) /wɔːk/. Drop the first sound completely so it rhymes with hawk. In words like (silk) /sɪlk/, remember to keep both sounds.
